lyrics.tag: soft piano, faint fellowship-hall room tone

lines: The last chord is still in the rafters,
coats half on in the slow-moving aisle,
the candles are out but the warmth is not,
so we linger together a while.
And the blessing don't end when the doors open wide,
it walks past the threshold and stays at our side —
After the amen, the grace goes home,
into the traffic, the supper, the phone,
the benediction was never the end,
it's the door He holds open again and again,
after the amen, we're not on our own.
Steam off the coffee in paper-thin cups,
an old hand held longer than manners require,
the sermon dissolves but the mercy holds up,
and the sanctuary follows us home.
After the amen, the grace goes home,

after the amen, we're not on our own.

lyrics.tag: soft piano, faint communion-rail room tone

lines: A torn loaf is passing from hand to hand,
the dark cup is catching the window's gold,
a stranger's thumb brushes crumbs where I stand,
and the aisle becomes kin as the story is told.
We kneel at the rail where the worn wood has shone,
and the emptiest hands are the ones He fills on —
Bread and wine, bread and wine,
the body was broken to make yours and mine,
poured like the morning, torn like the day,
He is the meal that we carry away,
bread and wine, and the guest is divine.
No banquet of silver, no cathedral of stone,
just a plate's little clink and a whispered amen,
but the King of the table won't eat it alone,
He sits down with sinners and calls them His friends.
Bread and wine, bread and wine,
the body was broken to make yours and mine,
poured like the morning, torn like the day,
He is the meal that we carry away,
bread and wine, and the guest is divine.
So I take what I never could earn or deserve,
the mercy that kneels down to sinners to serve,
and I rise from the rail with the taste of the vine —
remembered, forgiven, and no longer just mine.
bread and wine, and the guest is divine.
The pianist leaned on a note that's not written,
a small bending grace between two heavy chords,
and the wrong one I sang, He forgave into rhythm,
till the flaw found a home in the sound He restored.
For the note I could never have earned or have played,
He slips in the measure and calls it His way —
added in soft where my hands fell away,
He fills every rest that I leave in the song,
holds the whole broken bar where I couldn't belong,
The dust in the light where the last hymn had ended,
the silence that hummed when the organ let go,
even there He was writing the line I'd not tended,
the mercy between all the notes that I know.
added in soft where my hands fell away,
He fills every rest that I leave in the song,
holds the whole broken bar where I couldn't belong,
I am not the melody, clean and complete,
I'm the halting refrain and the missed downbeat,
but He scores every gap with a note I can't reach —
and the song is still saved by the grace in between.

Drums fade first, piano plays the opening figure once more and stops.

Rhodes pad fades in underneath holding a single warm chord.
Muffled kick and quiet brushes enter at a slow tempo, bass plays long sustained notes.
Vibraphone states the main melody, sparse and unhurried, each phrase followed by silence.

Drums stop, vibraphone plays the opening three notes again, reverb tail is left exposed.

Drums fade, flute holds a single long breathy note over piano and leaf texture.
Heavily filtered soul texture loops twice alone under thick vinyl crackle.
Punchy boom bap drums enter hard, sub bass locks to the kick immediately.

Loop drops out, drums and sub bass alone for eight bars.
Everything returns at full volume, filter fully open, most energetic point of the album.

Nylon guitar plays a bossa comping pattern alone, faint breeze and distant street ambience.

Vibraphone states the main melody in short phrases over the bossa pattern.
Guitar takes the melody itself, vibraphone answers with single sustained notes.
Drums thin to shaker only, bass walks a short solo line.
Full arrangement returns, vibraphone and guitar state the melody together.
Guitar returns to the opening comping pattern and slowly fades into outdoor ambience.
Rhodes plays two warm chords, faint page-turn texture and vinyl crackle underneath.
Low clarinet states a short woody phrase alone over the Rhodes.
Brushed drums and slow walking upright bass enter, groove settles into a soft swing.
Clarinet carries the full melody, Rhodes answers in the gaps between phrases.
Clarinet rests, Rhodes takes the melody with fuller voicings, bass walks more actively.
Clarinet and Rhodes state the melody in loose unison, paper textures slightly more audible.
Drums fade first, clarinet holds one long low note over the final Rhodes chord.
Rhodes plays a short question-like phrase panned left, silence after it.
Vibraphone answers the same phrase panned right, the two alternate once more.
Dusty drums and upright bass enter, the two voices begin trading over the groove.
Full melodic exchange between Rhodes and vibraphone, neither voice plays a complete melody alone.
Muted trumpet appears briefly, harmony lifts from E minor toward G major.
For the first time both voices play the melody in unison instead of trading.
Drums fade, Rhodes plays the opening phrase, vibraphone answers once and stops.
Room tone, thick vinyl crackle, one faint distant chair scrape, then a single piano chord.
Felt piano states the main melody with heavy sustain, no rhythm section at all.
Very quiet brushed snare enters, still no kick, piano continues with fuller voicings.
Melody expands into the upper register, reverb tail is at its longest here.
Brushes stop, piano returns to sparse single-line phrasing.
